new_statements.rule_in_words: The source does not say where the accent falls. It states only that the jargon has no grammar of its own but uses that of the local Qa'eni Persian dialect, and that word accentuation is weaker ('not so strong') than in Qa'eni Persian. By implication the accent pattern is that of the host Persian dialect, but Ivanow does not state a position.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the only prosodic remark concerns the relative weakness of the accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Remark is about word accentuation in general (isolated words elicited as a secret vocabulary); no distinction of word vs phrase level is made.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog classes casp1241 as an Iranian-based Speech Register (argot), not a language with its own grammar; its only two references are wordlists. Ivanow 1914 describes the secret jargon of the Gypsies (self-name Kauli; called Ustokor) of Qainat (Qa'en-Birjand, South Khorasan), whose matrix language is the local Qa'eni Persian dialect; Ivanow 1920 adds the Nishapur/Sabzavar variety. de Morgan 1904 gives bare vocabularies of 'Djougi' and 'Gooudari' nomads camped at Asterabad (Gorgan) on the Caspian. Any prosody is that of the host Persian dialect; this is distinct from Zargari Romani (European Romani spoken near Qazvin) and from the Domari-type 'Karachi' of Transcaucasia.
